_meta.honest_2022_view_note: At 2022-06-01 cutoff, the J-Book corpus (FY 2026 PEs from FY2024-2025 J-Books) returns NOT_FOUND_IN_TIMERANGE for nearly every SDA program because those FY rows post-date the cutoff. Per the framework, this means most program-level divergence signals are NOT YET VISIBLE in 2022; honest scoring is UNVERIFIABLE rather than manufactured SEVERE/RED. USAspending cross-checks DO confirm Redwire's subsidiaries received the contracts they implied (Roccor $27.8M, LoadPath $8 awards, MIS $87.6M Tipping Point, Redwire consolidated 189 awards / $397.6M).

scores.claim_text: Redwire designed and built deployable Link 16 antennas for Tranche 0 of the SDA proliferated LEO constellation.
supports: pentagon_jbook hit: SDA Transport Layer Tranches 0-2 (PE 1206410SF), status_declared FUNDED_SHRINKING per FY26 J-Book, but at 2022-06-01 cutoff signal=NOT_FOUND_IN_TIMERANGE (no funding rows yet visible).

usaspending confirms Roccor (Redwire Space Solutions LLC) received $27.8M across 10 DoD contracts including SCARLET deployable trusses and ATHENA deployable antennas — the contract substrate behind the claim is real.

Primary contractors named in the J-Book for the SDA Transport Layer are York/Lockheed/Northrop (prime bus integrators); Redwire/Roccor is a component sub (antennas), consistent with the claim's modest framing.
scores.M_value: NOT_FOUND_IN_TIMERANGE (FY26 status_declared = FUNDED_SHRINKING is POST-CUTOFF and excluded)
scores.interpretation: At the 2022 cutoff, the SDA Transport Layer was ramping (Tranche 0 launches were mid-2022 onward); J-Book de-funding signals were not yet visible. The claim is fact-grounded (Roccor did sub on T0 Link-16 antennas per usaspending). Honest 2022 score: PASS-leaning-UNVERIFIABLE — narrative-load is light (one-line bullet, not a revenue-concentration claim). Marked UNVERIFIABLE because the forward divergence cannot be confirmed at the cutoff.

overall_thesis_summary: At the 2022-06-01 cutoff, Redwire's S-1 narrative is dominated by NASA-funded programs (Archinaut/OSAM-2 = ~$73-87M, ROSA on ISS / Lunar Gateway, Solar Cruiser via Roccor) — the J-Book divergence pattern does not apply cleanly because NASA programs are outside the J-Book corpus and DoD/SDA programs that the company sub-contracted on (Tranche 0 Link-16 antennas via Roccor) had not yet reached the FY24-26 funding rows where the de-funding becomes visible. Honest 2022 verdict: NO J-Book divergence signal yet. Forward risks (SDA Transport Layer Tranche 3 declared UNFUNDED_TWO_PLUS_YEARS in FY26 J-Book, with replacement by SpaceX Starshield) would only become visible in 2024+. This is the framework correctly returning UNVERIFIABLE rather than manufacturing severity from post-cutoff knowledge.
